data.hook: Less than three weeks after signing veteran tackle D.J. Humphries for depth, the Washington Commanders cut him loose on Friday. They quickly turned to practice-squad lineman Julian Good-Jones for the season opener.
data.name: Commanders Release D.J. Humphries, Elevate Good-Jones Before Opener
data.summary: The Commanders released 32-year-old Humphries, a former Pro Bowl pick with the Cardinals, ahead of Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. This avoids guaranteeing his full 2026 salary and clears room for younger talent like third-rounder Brandon Coleman at left tackle. Good-Jones, an undrafted veteran familiar with the interior line, steps up as added depth at center or guard. The moves leave Washington with three tackles on the 53-man roster as they head into a tough road test.

data.summary: The 26-second video from Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026, showed the team in burgundy jerseys handling the ball during pregame warm-ups ahead of Week 1. Fans and ex-player Anthony Armstrong defended it as a common way to add variety, loosen up, and calm nerves, much like the Washington Capitals' 'sewer ball' routine. Similar scenes appeared near the Eagles sideline and Chargers practices, showing it's standard across NFL settings, though some criticized the reporter's skeptical caption.

data.hook: Jalen Hurts dropped three touchdown passes, and the defense stuffed a game-winning two-point try to hand the Eagles a narrow victory at home.
data.name: Eagles Edge Commanders 24-22 in Season Opener Thriller
data.summary: Philadelphia beat Washington 24-22 at Lincoln Financial Field to open the 2026 NFL season 1-0. Hurts went 14-of-25 for 203 yards with scores to Dallas Goedert twice and debutant Dontayvion Wicks, who snagged a 64-yard bomb and a 9-yard touchdown. Jayden Daniels rallied the Commanders late with a touchdown to make it 24-22, but Moro Ojomo stopped the two-point conversion. Hurts praised the team's passion, execution, and focus after the win, as Philly eyes the Titans next.

data.name: Eagles Edge Commanders 24-22 in Opener as Hits Steal Spotlight
data.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles kicked off their season with a 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field, thanks to Hurts' 203 yards and scores to Dallas Goedert twice and rookie Dontayvion Wicks on a 64-yard bomb and 9-yard touchdown. Washington rallied late with Jayden Daniels' two fourth-quarter touchdowns, including a 1-yard score to Antonio Williams, but Philly stopped the two-point try to hold on. Defensive standouts like rookie linebacker Sonny Styles' massive hit and Tyler Owens' special teams play drew endless replays, memes calling them a 'menace' and 'the Hulk,' while the Eagles celebrated their 'DUB.'

data.hook: With the season opener minutes away, the Eagles cleared up their biggest roster mystery: veteran Andy Dalton steps in as backup to Jalen Hurts.
data.name: Eagles Name Andy Dalton as Jalen Hurts' Backup for Season Opener
data.summary: Philadelphia released its inactives list ahead of Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field, confirming third-year Tanner McKee as the emergency third quarterback while Cole Payton, wide receiver Elijah Moore, outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard, and guard Micah Morris also sit out. The choice ends weeks of speculation, as coach Nick Sirianni had held off naming a clear QB2 to keep opponents guessing. Greenard, a recent offseason addition, remains sidelined by a pectoral injury despite limited practice, leaving the Eagles mostly healthy for the NFC East matchup.

data.hook: With the clock winding down and the Steelers up by seven, Darnell Washington caught a pass and unleashed a massive stiff arm that flattened Falcons defender Xavier Watts.
data.name: Darnell Washington's Stiff Arm Seals Steelers Win Over Falcons
data.summary: The 6-foot-7, 311-pound tight end powered through Watts on third-and-3 late in the fourth quarter, gaining crucial yardage to seal Pittsburgh's 20-13 victory. Fans and media lit up with reactions like Barstool Sports calling it putting a man 'THROUGH THE EARTH' and the Steelers posting 'GROWN MAN 💪'. The play highlighted Washington's physical style in a defense-dominated game that also featured T.J. Watt's pick-six.
